facts.fact: The Ministry of Public Health's DHIS2 plan states that a nationwide generic HMIS is in place for aggregate data with data entry at the facility level, scoring aggregate data 70% in a maturity self-assessment of 117 indicators, while facilities still fill paper registers and monthly reporting booklets that the plan budgets to reprint for 6,200 facilities; dated to the plan, April 2022.

The ministry's plan describes DHIS2 as the national health data repository and a nationwide generic HMIS fed by the monthly activity report of health facilities, in a country it counts as having 197 health districts and 6,200 facilities, and refers to a separate hospital form; it does not break use down by facility level.

The ministry's plan gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports: it says work remains on completeness and timeliness, and plans data entry incentives for the data managers of 6,200 facilities and one laptop or tablet per facility, each reaching 20% of users a year.

The plan names the ministry's Health Information Unit as in charge of the HMIS on the data side and its Information Technology Unit on the infrastructure side, under a ministerial decree setting up a DHIS2 governance body; the server is hosted by BAO Systems under an annual contract of USD 19,200, with a plan to mirror and later relocate it to Cameroon.

The Ministry of Public Health issued a DHIS2 Operational Plan for 2022 to 2024 costed at USD 19,412,966, of which USD 830,000 is technical assistance; it reports that the plan it replaces was 31% executed, with 17% of 90 activities completed and 54% not started.

The plan names no source of funds for its USD 19.4 million: its financing section says resource mobilisation will continue, its conclusion calls for investment and alignment from donors, and it attributes the previous plan's shortfall partly to activities not matching the funding available.
